description: A box-shadow with a real declared blur radius, validating this crate's own hand-rolled Gaussian blur against Chromium's real rendering — no text, so pixel comparison is this fixture's precise signal.

classification.reason: Two independent Gaussian blur implementations (this crate's own hand-rolled one vs. Chromium's) never round every pixel identically along the shadow's own soft gradient — but how far they diverge depends on which of Chromium's own rendering backends actually draws the blur. Against a GPU-accelerated Chromium (this fixture's own author, and a real desktop's `florui compare`): 4.68% differing pixels, every single one off by exactly 1 out of 255 (max_error: 1, mean_error: 0.0468) — sub-perceptible rounding noise. Against the identical pinned Chromium binary running headless on a GPU-less CI runner (falls back to software/SwiftShader rendering, a materially different blur compositing path than GPU rendering takes): 13.0% differing pixels, max_error 2, mean_error 0.1355 — geometry still an exact 60x60 match both times, so this is rendering-backend divergence in Chromium itself, not a shape/position bug in this crate. Calibrated to the higher, CI-measured number plus real margin, not the friendlier desktop one.
